description:
pkix-ct/src/sct.rs:208-250 — internal Cursor type with hand-rolled read_u8 / read_u16_be / read_u64_be / read_u16_prefixed methods. Refuses to pull in nom or byteorder for what's essentially a 40-line plumbing helper.

A future contributor might suggest 'use nom for cleaner parsing.' Adding nom would:
- Add ~300KB to the compiled crate per nom version churn.
- Drag in error-type machinery (nom::error::*) that doesn't compose with this crate's Error type.
- Make the no_std contract more fragile (nom is no_std but the macro stack changes between versions).

The current Cursor is 40 lines, bounds-checks, returns Result<&[u8]>, and is trivially auditable. No engineering basis to prefer nom or byteorder for parsers this small.

Marked opinion because the choice is taste; what's NOT taste is the 'no needless deps' principle that picks the right outcome here. Defend the manual cursor against 'simplification' suggestions.
title: Cursor-based bytes parser is no_std-friendly and avoids dependencies on byteorder or nom
